target.title: fix(github-copilot): keep device login polling within GitHub limits
target.body:
Closes #64319

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users signing in to GitHub Copilot could remain rate-limited until their device code expired after GitHub returned `slow_down`. The device-login loop waited only two extra seconds and then reverted to the original cadence, while GitHub requires a cumulative five-second increase for every later poll.

## Why This Change Was Made

The GitHub Copilot plugin now retains the increased poll interval for the rest of the device flow, applies GitHub's required five-second increase on each `slow_down`, and honors a larger valid interval returned by the server. The change stays in the provider-owned login loop; endpoints, token storage, public configuration, and other providers are unchanged.

This PR is AI-assisted. The implementation and official protocol contract were reviewed before publication.

## User Impact

GitHub Copilot device login can recover from rate-limit backoff without repeatedly polling too quickly or waiting until the authorization code expires.

## Evidence

- Official GitHub contract: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps#rate-limits-for-the-device-flow
- Standards contract: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628.html#section-3.5
- Before fix, the deterministic Testbox sequence failed with token polls at 0, 3, 4, and 7 seconds instead of the required 0, 9, 18, and 32 seconds (12 passed, 1 failed).
- After fix, the focused test passes 13/13 and the complete GitHub Copilot extension suite passes 123/123 on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx57xj1hxqcsetznzj856g63`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed remotely for both changed files, including extension production/test typechecks, focused lint, architecture guards, and import-cycle checks.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed.
- Fresh structured autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.
- No credentialed GitHub login was performed; the regression uses an exact fake-timer request sequence and exercises the production polling state machine.
